Subject: Unexpected spike: duplicate session counts in June invoice

Hi Logan,

We just reviewed our June invoice and noticed a ~3x jump in token/session charges between Jun 10-14 that doesn't line up with our traffic or deploys. Attached is a small sample of our client-side logs for that period (usage-sample-logs.csv). Can you take a look and explain what caused the spike?

Key points:
- Account: CleverApps (CLV-3789)
- Invoice: June 2027 (attached) shows $9,450 this month vs $3,200 typical
- We didn't rollout any new batch jobs or increase concurrency during that window

Would appreciate a quick triage and, if this is an error, a provisional credit while you investigate.

Hi all,

I pulled the raw telemetry and attached a trimmed export (redwood-raw-telemetry.jsonl) focusing on request IDs and stream/batch toggles for Jun 9-16. Quick summary of findings so far:

- We see a cluster of requests from CLV-3789 where the client produced identical request_id values across separate TCP connections around 2027-06-11T03:20:00Z. That pattern led to the KV-cache being used multiple times and duplicated token attribution on our aggregation window.
- Two contributing factors:
  1) A recent client-side retry policy (backoff disabled) that restarted the same logical session without regenerating a new request_id.
  2) Our streaming-to-batch attribution window (default 10s) had a race when the same request_id arrives on two different workers; both workers committed partial counts before the dedupe reconciler ran.

This combination can produce duplicated counts until the reconciler consolidates. That reconciliation usually happens within 24–72 hours, but if the client logs are re-ingested as separate sessions it can persist through the billing window.

Immediate mitigation we can apply:
- We can run a retroactive dedupe pass for CLV-3789 for Jun 10-14. That will correct attribution and reduce billed tokens.
- We'll need the client-side request_id sample (Samir sent one file) and ideally a sample of the TCP timestamps so we can correlate exact arrivals.

I'll start the dedupe job as soon as we have confirmation and the extra sample. If you want, we can also apply a one-time provisional credit to clear the overage while the job runs.

Marcus Lin
Billing Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
